security.evidence: Every ability resolves the caller's membership server-side from the model, never from request input (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:30-40 uses membershipFor/isManager, app/Policies/EntityMembershipPolicy.php:30-41); no unescaped output, no raw SQL, no secrets; fillable lists are explicit. scope.evidence: Diff contains only models, enum, policies, migrations, factories, tests, and the docs/changelog updates the task/conventions ask for (docs/database-schema.md, docs/README.md, CHANGELOG.md); nothing from the out-of-scope list (task.md:58-63: routes, pages, session, middleware) appears.

issues.explanation: assignRole only checks whether the caller is owner/admin of the entity and never inspects the target membership, so an admin can change the owner membership's role (demoting the owner and leaving the entity ownerless) and nothing in the policy restricts assignment to UserRole::manageable() values.
The entities block still lists locale_default even though the doc now says the tenant model is implemented and the entities migration does not create that column, so the docs overstate what exists.
The change rewrites an already-recorded entry under a previous release (drops "and circular FK note for owner") instead of only adding an entry under [Unreleased], which edits release history.
There is no case asserting what should happen when assignRole targets the owner membership, which is why the policy gap above is not caught by the suite.

review.summary: The change implements the tenant persistence and authorization layer as specified: two migrations (including the portable stored owner_seq column with its named unique indexes), the Entity/EntityMembership/UserRole/User models with relations, scopes and casts, both policies, factories, and a thorough Pest suite, with the schema docs and changelog updated. It is well scoped, idiomatic and tested; the only substantive concern is that EntityMembershipPolicy::assignRole does not protect the owner membership or restrict assignable roles, plus a small docs drift on locale_default. That warrants approval with minor changes rather than as-is.
